svg.text: Ch'alish P'ilam, the ceremonial hand — the canon and a pilot
Every glyph is its own picture, drawn whole inside a cushion that always stands round it. Two brushes: the contour brush, 32 units, and the detail brush, 20.
Heads face the line's start. The kit of recurring parts gives the hand its look; no glyph is built from a skeleton. Drawn from tools/chalish-pilam/ceremonial.py.
a narrow affix before a sign
a flattened affix over a sign
The pilot glyphs: full, half and double footprints; cushion, round cartouche and free silhouette
the patriarch: MAN, HIGH and HOUSE made one · full
the 260-day count, a day in its cartouche · full
The core concepts (with SUN, MOON and WATER above)
Precomposed concepts: what the common hand writes with two or three glyphs, drawn as one
The gods: one glyph each, as complicated as it needs to be
Rank and office: a head wearing the regalia of its office
The city-states: each city's emblem, its picture with the beaded seat of rule; the unruled land has none
a burial, going into the earth · ye
Kul'qat Tik'il, a foundation laid · ku
The syllabary: every syllable's signs, flat (above or below a sign) and tall (before or after it); red: traditional sounds
Composed blocks: a name is a house emblem, syllable signs and a coefficient, written in codage
three; la over the emblem, compact
the name runs on: sho, bi
An inscription in paired columns, packed by footprint as a page wraps it: two blocks to a row
on the thirteenth day of the count;
Blocks beside Monaspace Neon at 48 and 24 px, set as the font sets them: spanning descender to ascender
